weekend_summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli took pole (1:34.035) and converted it to a commanding 56-lap US Grand Prix victory, 13.078s ahead of Charles Leclerc, with Max Verstappen third. Mercedes executed a one-stop medium-to-hard strategy; Ferrari and several rivals used two stops. The final order was affected by a Russell time penalty, grid penalties and three retirements. LatentLap's retrospectively generated race forecast ranked the entire points-paying top 10 correctly and had 1.8-place overall classification MAE. This is retrospective diagnostic agreement, not a real-time pre-race forecast.

Q.summary: Antonelli secured pole in 1:34.035, Verstappen P2 (+0.179s), Hadjar P3, Leclerc P4 and Hamilton P5. Russell was P6; Norris' fastest Q3 lap was deleted for track limits.

key_moments.text: Antonelli set a 1:34.035 pole lap, 0.179s clear of Verstappen.
Hadjar qualified third; Russell sixth, and Norris had a lap deleted for track limits.

R.summary: Antonelli won by 13.078s on a one-stop strategy. Leclerc charged to P2 after a late stop, passing Verstappen; Hamilton finished fourth and Norris fifth. Bottas, Colapinto and Bearman retired.

key_moments.text: Antonelli completed 56 laps and led Leclerc by 13.078s at the finish.
Leclerc passed Norris and Verstappen late to take second, while Hamilton took fourth.
Bottas' late stop on track triggered a Virtual Safety Car.
Russell served a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

ANT.name: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
ANT.summary: Pole, dominant one-stop win and an exact P1 retrospective pace forecast.

details.text: Race result supports a strong Austin performance; the theoretical ERS model does not reveal actual battery state.

LEC.name: Charles Leclerc
LEC.summary: Qualified fourth and advanced to second after a strong two-stop race and late overtakes.

details.text: A new floor/bodywork package was declared, but the race cannot isolate its causal lap-time gain.

VER.name: Max Verstappen
VER.summary: Started second and finished third; experienced drivability and engine-braking concerns.

details.text: P3 matched the retrospective race forecast, but race execution and technical issues affected the order.

RUS.name: George Russell
RUS.summary: Finished eighth after a five-second penalty, despite the same overall upgraded-car configuration as Antonelli.

details.text: Russell's P8 classification is not a clean measurement of Mercedes peak pace.

NOR.name: Lando Norris
NOR.summary: A late strategic gamble and worn tyres cost Norris positions; finished fifth.

details.text: He was passed late by Verstappen, Leclerc and Hamilton; finish position combines race management and pace.

Mercedes.summary: Antonelli won on a successful one-stop; Russell finished eighth after an incident penalty.

details.text: The race does not support applying Antonelli's whole performance improvement as a causal upgrade gain.

Ferrari.summary: Leclerc finished second and Hamilton fourth after two-stop races, coinciding with a declared broad aero package.

details.text: Upgrade presence and result correlation are not enough to estimate causal upgrade benefit.

Red Bull.summary: Verstappen finished third, Hadjar sixth, with race drivability/mapping issues.

details.text: The declared Red Bull front-wing vane was evaluation-focused; avoid assuming a known performance step.

McLaren.summary: Norris P5 and Piastri P7; late tyre management shaped finishing order.

details.text: New front/rear corner and diffuser changes were declared; no isolated gain is established.

strategy_and_conditions.text: The Grand Prix was run in dry conditions; the R18 race representative pace can be part of normal dry-race history if the local pipeline quality checks passed.
Antonelli completed a one-stop medium-to-hard race; Leclerc and several rivals used two stops.
Two Virtual Safety Car periods occurred, including a late one triggered by Bottas' retirement.
The official starting grid included penalties for Lindblad, Colapinto, Bortoleto and a pit-lane start for Stroll.
Russell's five-second time penalty was imposed during the race rather than before it; do not treat it as a grid penalty.

performance_interpretation.text: Antonelli's qualifying pole and race win are independent evidence of strong competitive performance at COTA, but cannot identify true ERS usage.
The retrospective forecast matched all ten points finishers as a set. Preserve it as a backtest result, not contemporaneous pre-race model validation.
Rain-excluded Malaysia R/Singapore S sessions were not supposed to contribute to this dry-race forecast; inspect local prediction history for leakage if auditing reproducibility.

upgrades_and_technical_context.text: Both drivers return to latest Sepang-spec package: Mercedes declared no NEW Austin components. Russell and Antonelli were confirmed to run the current upgraded car after split-spec Singapore; existing R16 persistent event already carries this weight. R17 front-wing was a Singapore practice trial, not a Singapore race upgrade; no extra weight assigned here.

prediction_review.overall_assessment: Retrospective race ranking matched all ten points finishers as a set and recorded 1.8-place classification MAE (1.2 excluding three retirements). Qualifying position MAE was 2.0. These are post-event diagnostics, not a live-timestamped pre-race prediction.

successes.text: Antonelli predicted P1 for the Grand Prix and won, converting pole to victory with a one-stop strategy.
Leclerc and Verstappen finished P2 and P3 exactly as the saved race forecast ranked them.
All ten points finishers were identified by the race forecast: True; 8 of 22 classified places matched exactly.

misses.text: Colapinto's retirement increased his position error to +9 places; a retirement is not a clean pace observation.
Bearman and Bottas also retired; all three retirements distort race position errors.
Russell received a five-second race penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, separate from pre-race grid penalties.

known_exceptions.text: The saved R18 forecasts were generated retrospectively after the weekend, but before local R18 results ingestion; do not label them a live pre-race prediction.
The comparison uses classified finishing order, not a measured steady-state dry pace reference or true ERS power trace.
Grid and race penalties explain classification differences but do not reorder modelled pace outputs.

knowledge_limits.text: Formula 1 actual ERS harvest and battery state are not public; LatentLap ERS values are inferred/theoretical.
Single-session pace differences confound fuel, tyre age, traffic, strategy and track state.
Declared upgrades do not prove their isolated effectiveness.
R18 forecast is retrospective; do not use its classification MAE to claim prospective out-of-sample performance.
